question:
This ticket machine works great for some people and not at all for others. Find out who would struggle, and what is getting in their way.

Steps:
1. Use the arrow tool to connect at least 2 people to the feature that would cause them trouble.
2. Place a shape on the person who would have no trouble.
3. Record your voice with one change that would help the most people.

rubric.description: No arrow or shape is placed on the board, or the voice recording is missing or blank.
Student places fewer than 2 arrows, OR the arrows do not match a feature to a person it affects.

At least 2 arrows connect a resident to the feature that causes trouble (A to 1, B to 2, C to 3, or E to 1 or 4) AND a shape is on D AND the voice recording names one change that would help most people.
Meets all of the above AND the voice recording says who was probably missing when the machine was designed or tested.

whiteboard_starter_image_alt_text: "A train station adds a new AI ticket machine." A drawing of the machine shows a touchscreen labeled "TICKETS," a "card only" slot, and a "voice help" button. Its four numbered features: 1, touchscreen only, no buttons; 2, the screen is in English only; 3, card payments only; and 4, voice help talks fast and cannot repeat. Five people: A, Mr. Chen, 82, has trouble seeing small touchscreens; B, Aisha moved here last month and is learning English; C, Dev is a student who only has cash; D, Lena commutes daily, speaks fluent English, and has a card; and E, Omar is blind and uses a screen reader.
